title: Stage B: the core shapes generated by a PydanticGenerator subclass over S4's core.yaml
question: Can a linkml 1.12.1 PydanticGenerator subclass (or an own emitter) over S4's core.yaml produce the core shapes of values.py and batch.py: discriminated t/op unions with a named recursive Condition, MISSING defaults (pydantic 2.14.1), frozen models with tuples, both ci:form variants (authored/stored) and prefixed aliases; how does the result differ structurally from the hand shapes, do S4's 135 batches validate alike, and are the JSON Schemas byte-identical to core/schemas/*.json?
answers: model-and-projections §3.3 Stage B or its fallback
method: S4's core.yaml copied and patched (code/q1/model_patch.yaml: condition node classes, batch items, evidence, qualifiers class, envelope, types and enums; Expression base; interval bounds; class order) to results/q1/schema/core_stage_b.yaml and linted with S4's config; code/q1/stage_b.py, a PydanticGenerator subclass with template_dir overrides (frozen CoreModel, PEP 695 type aliases, explicit Field sources), overriding _get_classes, generate_class, generate_slot, get_class_slot_range and before_generate_enums, with a form-expansion plan over SchemaView (ci:form, ci:required_in, ci:stored_range); behaviour as hand hooks (code/q1/hooks.py) named by a proposed ci:validator, span and presence rules generated from ci:invariant. The generated module is compared with the product's values.py/batch.py (read-only import): per-class fields, defaults, aliases, exclude_if, config, bases, validators, the four union aliases; JSON Schemas rendered with the product's CoreJsonSchema against the committed files; S4's 135 batches as written, after S4's V1/V2 canonicalization and (stored) after a probe-local prefix migration, validated by both model sets (verdicts, (loc, type) error sets, dumps); 12 seeded errors; stock gen-pydantic over the same schema for contrast; regeneration determinism.

inputs.role: model patch, generator subclass, templates, hand hooks

outputs.role: patched schema and lint, generated module and stock output, generated JSON Schemas, structure/schema/batch/seeded comparisons, summary, run log

results.name: features_present
results.note: named recursive AuthoredCondition $defs with op discriminator, t discriminator, MISSING default and absent dump, frozen, extra forbid, tuples, both forms, stored-only fields, core: aliases, defaults excluded

results.name: classes_structurally_equal
results.note: the other 10 differ in base class (hand private bases _Batch, _Claim, _Entity, _Qualifiers, _Span are flattened), AuthoredQualifiers field order, and NumberValue (pattern instead of the hand canonical-decimal validator)

results.name: hand_classes_not_generated

results.name: json_schemas_byte_equal

results.name: json_schemas_equal_without_descriptions

results.name: batch_validations_agree
results.note: 135 batches; verdict and (loc, type) error set equal in every case

results.name: valid_dumps_equal
results.note: 17 authored, 120 stored after the probe-local prefix migration

results.name: seeded_errors_rejected_by_both
results.note: 11 with equal error sets; non-canonical number: value_error (hand) vs string_pattern_mismatch (generated)

results.name: stock_gen_pydantic_discriminators
results.note: stock output: no discriminator, no MISSING, no tuples, one class per model class with both forms' fields optional

conclusion: The Stage B variant is feasible as a PydanticGenerator subclass: over a patched S4 core.yaml it generates every shape of values.py and the items, evidence, qualifiers and envelopes of batch.py, with the four discriminated union aliases identical to the hand ones, MISSING defaults, frozen tuples, both ci:form variants and core: aliases; all 300 validations of S4's 135 batches agree with the hand models in verdict and error set, and valid dumps are identical. What the subclass keeps from PydanticGenerator is its pipeline and template machinery; class and slot generation are overridden and the form expansion is own code over SchemaView, so it is close to an own emitter hosted in the generator. Residue: the model needs the condition nodes, items and envelope declared (TM §2), an Expression base, typed interval bounds, a declaration order matching the unions, and proposed ci:py_type, ci:validator and ci:py_name annotations; hand private bases flatten (their methods, e.g. _Batch.local_refs used by tests, become functions); CitationFrame stays hand; the canonical-decimal check changes error type unless kept as a hand validator with a schema-only pattern; the committed JSON Schemas are not byte-equal because their descriptions are hand docstrings, otherwise equal except the authored qualifiers' property order.
